title: Green wins Hockenheim finale as BMW takes the manufacturers’ crown
dek: Jamie Green passed pole-sitter Gary Paffett and won the final race by 1.351 seconds in an Audi 1-2-3, finishing runner-up to Pascal Wehrlein while BMW took the manufacturers’ title by seven points.

chapters.title: Second place and the manufacturers’ title remain
text: Saturday had settled the drivers’ title. Timo Scheider won Race 1 for Audi, and Pascal Wehrlein’s eighth place took him to 169 points, 40 clear of Mattias Ekström with only 25 left to win, making him the youngest champion in DTM history on the eve of his 21st birthday. What remained on Sunday was the fight for second place, with Ekström on 129, Edoardo Mortara on 128 and Jamie Green on 125, and the manufacturers’ title, where BMW led Audi by 56 points after Race 1. The finale was an hour plus one lap and included a compulsory pit stop.

chapters.title: Paffett takes pole on his last lap
text: Conditions were dry and the field ran on slicks. Gary Paffett improved on his final flying lap to put the Euronics/BWT Mercedes on pole with 1m32.645s. Green was 0.038s behind in the Rosberg Audi, and Ekström (1m32.729s) and Miguel Molina (1m32.746s), both of Audi Sport Team Abt Sportsline, made up the second row. Maxime Martin’s BMW, on 1m32.826s, was fifth and the best of the BMWs.

Adrien Tambay, Nico Müller and Scheider took the next three places for Audi, so that the first eight cars on the grid held six Audis, and Maximilian Götz and Augusto Farfus completed the top ten, with the whole group covered by 0.331s. Mortara, who needed to make up ground, qualified only 13th, ahead of Mike Rockenfeller, Bruno Spengler and Marco Wittmann. The new champion, Wehrlein, started 17th, António Félix da Costa 19th and Christian Vietoris last in 24th.

chapters.title: Green and Ekström overhaul Paffett
text: Paffett led away from pole, but Green’s start was sluggish and Ekström dropped behind Martin at the start. Green made his move on lap four with a clean pass on Paffett at the hairpin, and had a lead of about 1.2s by the end of that lap. Ekström followed him through, passing Martin and then Paffett within a few laps, and the two Audis settled into first and second. Marco Wittmann, the reigning champion, was out after seven laps.

chapters.title: Mortara’s late stop pays off
text: Green kept the lead through the stop window apart from a brief spell after his own stop, and stayed about three seconds clear of Ekström. The race was changed by those who stayed out. Mortara was the last to come in, set a string of fast laps in clean air and rejoined fifth, then passed Scheider and Paul di Resta in the second half of the race. His quickest lap, a 1m34.086s on lap 25, was the fastest of the race.

Trouble came on the run to the hairpin after the stops, when Vietoris’s Mercedes clashed with Molina’s Audi, spun and hit Tambay. Both Vietoris and Tambay were out after 15 laps, and Molina was given a drive-through penalty and recovered to only 11th. Wehrlein, starting from 17th, spent the afternoon in the thick of the contact, with a fierce scrap with Müller at the hairpin that left his car battered.

chapters.title: Green wins, Mortara completes the podium
text: Green took the flag 1.351s clear of Ekström, who closed to within two seconds late on but could not get close enough to try a pass, and the Audis filled the podium as Mortara came through from 13th to third, 18.914s behind the winner. Di Resta was fourth, the best of the Mercedes drivers, ahead of Scheider.

Behind them Martin took sixth after a battle with da Costa, who had charged up from 19th to seventh, ahead of Spengler. Paffett, who lamented a lack of rear grip, fell back to ninth after fighting Martin around the stops, and Martin Tomczyk took the last point in tenth. Wehrlein finished 20th.

chapters.title: Audi wins the race but not the titles
text: Green’s fourth win of the year, the most of any driver in 2015, lifted him to second in the championship on 150 points, 19 behind Wehrlein. He admitted that finishing as runner-up was a pity, but said the season had still been a strong one for the car and that he had enjoyed driving it again. Ekström finished third on 147, three points behind him, and Mortara fourth on 143, seven back, with Spengler fifth on 123 and Wittmann sixth on 112.

Audi won both races of the finale weekend, Scheider on Saturday and Green on Sunday, and left Hockenheim with ten wins from the 18 races, more than BMW and Mercedes managed between them, and with four of the first five places on Sunday, yet it won none of the three titles on offer. BMW took the manufacturers’ crown with 602 points to Audi’s 595, after Martin, da Costa, Spengler and Tomczyk all scored in the top ten. Mercedes finished third, and HWA took the teams’ title with Wehrlein and Vietoris.

Wehrlein’s Sunday contrasted sharply with his Saturday. After the scrap with Müller he finished 20th with a damaged car and no points, and said there was not much he could do and that he was glad to have brought it home before turning to the party with his team. A day after clinching the title, and on his 21st birthday, he collected the champion’s trophy, the first Mercedes driver to take the title since di Resta in 2010. The best Mercedes in the race was di Resta in fourth, while Paffett, who had led the opening laps from pole, ended up ninth. Scheider, the winner of Race 1, took fifth on Sunday, and Martin, pole-sitter on Saturday and third in Race 1, was the top BMW in sixth.

The finale closed a season of nine race weekends and 18 races, with two races on each weekend. With the champion known after Saturday, the closing hour was about second place and the manufacturers’ title, and both were settled by the chequered flag.

facts.t: Green ends the year with a win
facts.v: Green led home an Audi 1-2-3 by 1.351s from Ekström, his fourth win of the season, and finished second in the standings.
